subject: NYT: Investigating Omar Is ‘Authoritarian,’ But Prosecuting Trump Is ‘Accountability’
posts:
When elite editorial boards flip their definition of 'accountability' based entirely on party lines, free speech becomes a partisan shield.
Evidence: Selective outrage, Partisan double standards, Ideological protectionism
#Aletheia #MediaBias

The New York Times editorial board claims that investigating Rep. Ilhan Omar for potential immigration fraud is a chilling authoritarian assault on free speech.
Stated Judgement: (+0.80, +0.50) — Greater Good

Yet the same board championed sweeping criminal prosecutions against Donald Trump as essential accountability, revealing a flexible standard driven by partisan convenience.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.88, -0.82) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.
When institutional watchdogs abandon consistent principles to protect political allies, they sacrifice epistemic integrity for tribal loyalty.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 13.5, z: 4)

- The New York Times Editorial Board: FAIL (-0.88, -0.82) — Deploys 'free speech' selectively to shield political allies.
- Partisan Double Standards: FAIL (-0.82, -0.78) — Equates equal law enforcement with authoritarianism.
The debate highlights a stark polarization over whether political figures should face identical investigative scrutiny regardless of their party affiliation.

The Bright Side:
Exposing these glaring hypocrisies forces a much-needed public reckoning on journalistic integrity and the weaponization of high-minded rhetoric.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing standard legal investigations into potential fraud with 'authoritarian repression' mixes up basic institutional accountability with partisan grievance.

Social Physics Analysis:
The editorial board runs a smart selfish maneuver: wrapping political protectionism in the noble language of free speech while deploying partisan projection to discredit legitimate inquiries.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When lofty principles are inverted into partisan shields, it plots a direct course toward institutional decay and moral hypocrisy.

The Unavoidable Truth: Rules must apply equally to all politicians regardless of party.

The Unavoidable Lie: Investigating political fraud is only authoritarian when it targets your allies.

Alethekanon:
When sacred principles like free speech are weaponized solely as partisan shields, institutional credibility collapses under the weight of its own hypocrisy.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts public trust when powerful voices bend the truth for their own side, leaving everyday people confused and deeply cynical about fairness.

Brothekanon:
Rules for thee but not for me is getting pretty old when everyone can see right through the obvious double standards.

Spirithekanon:
"Woe to those who call evil good and good evil." Isaiah 5:20 FAIL
Selective morality blinds the heart to truth.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
NYT: Investigating Omar Is ‘Authoritarian,’ But Prosecuting Trump Is ‘Accountability’

Notably, the editorial board acknowledges it has no idea whether the allegations 'have merit.'

Actual Article Body:
The New York Times’ editorial board has found a dangerous, “authoritarian” threat to the republic: investigating a politician. Readers may remember a different approach The Times’ editorial board took when the politician was Donald Trump.

“Trump Is Turning to an Old Tool of Authoritarian Repression,” headlined an editorial board op-ed Friday, warning in the article’s opening line that “[t]he revocation of a political opponent’s citizenship has long been a tool of authoritarian repression.”

The story comes as Democrat Rep. Ilhan Omar is under federal investigation for alleged immigration fraud. According to The New York Post, Omar’s legal name is “Ilhan Nur Said Elmi,” yet she used the name Ilhan Omar on passports and other official documents. Further, the congresswoman could not definitely state whether she married her brother in a recent interview, whom she is alleged to have married illegally to get a green card.

This investigation into whether Omar illegally obtained U.S. citizenship, the board writes, “should disturb all Americans, regardless of whether they agree with Ms. Omar’ political views.”

“The investigation of her is a chilling example of the federal government using its immense power to silence a critic,” the board intones. “It is an affront to free speech, the rule of law and American ideals.”

This line of argument would grant immunity for any crime for any person who prominently criticizes the government. If it’s an “affront to free speech” to prosecute people based on factual evidence of lawbreaking, criticizing the government becomes a get-out-of-jail-free card.

We didn’t see The New York Times editorial board apply this reasoning to any critic of Joe Biden’s regime, such as lockdown and Covid shot dissenters. The Times said nothing about “authoritarian repression” when Biden imposed a mass censorship regime on the nation to silence its critics. It’s clear that, to the Times, words like “free speech” and “authoritarianism” have no fixed meaning but are wielded solely as emotional button-pushing sticks to suppress the left’s political enemies. What’s more “authoritarian” than that?

Notably, the editorial board also acknowledges it has no idea whether the allegations “have merit”: “Mr. Trump’s allies have claimed, among other things, that Ms. Omar’s father misrepresented her age during her naturalization process 26 years ago by saying she was 17 — and thus still a child — rather than 18. We do not pretend to know whether the allegations have merit. Yet as tempting as it may be to focus on them, they are not the main issue.”

Obviously whether the allegations have merit is key to determining whether the investigation is political or justly targeting possible illegal activity. The Times, however, instead pretends trying to discern the truth is a distraction from the conclusion they reached without caring about the facts — that applying the law equally, irrespective of title or fame, is an “unjust” prosecution.

When Trump faced sprawling investigations and prosecutions in 2023, however, The New York Times editorial board supported them, insisting no one is above the law, including politicians. “Even Donald Trump Should Be Held Accountable,” the same editorial board wrote in March 2023, as Trump faced bankruptcy and up to 110 years in prison on politicized charges.

“Donald Trump spent years as a candidate, in office and out of office, ignoring democratic and legal norms and precedents, trying to bend the Justice Department and the judiciary to his whims and behaving as if rules didn’t apply to him,” the board wrote then. “As the news of the indictment shows, they do.”

The Times’ editorial board proclaimed Trump’s indictment was evidence that the justice system was working since Trump thought the “rules didn’t apply to him.”

“A pattern of disregard for the law often leads to a criminal indictment, and that is the outcome Mr. Trump now faces,” the board intoned.

“A healthy respect for the legal system also requires Americans to set aside their politics when forming judgments on these cases,” the board continued. “The cost of failing to seek justice against a leader who may have committed these crimes would be higher still.”

Elmi is a Democrat instead of a Republican. Apparently to the Times’ editorial board, that alone should put her above the law.
